questions.stem: What is the solution set of the equation |x + 3| = 10 ?
questions.explanation: Split into two cases: x + 3 = 10 gives x = 7, and x + 3 = −10 gives x = −13. The solution set is {−13, 7}. Choice {−7, 13} comes from applying the sign change to the 3 instead of to the 10, and {−10, 10} ignores the shift entirely.
questions.verify:
sols=sorted(x for x in range(-100,101) if abs(x+3)==10)
"{"+", ".join(str(s).replace("-","−") for s in sols)+"}"

questions.stem: What is the greatest solution of the equation |3x − 5| = 13 ?
questions.explanation: The positive case 3x − 5 = 13 gives 3x = 18, so x = 6; the negative case 3x − 5 = −13 gives x = −8/3. The greater of the two is 6. Choice 18 stops at 3x = 18 without dividing by 3.
questions.verify:
from fractions import Fraction
s=[Fraction(13+5,3),Fraction(-13+5,3)]
str(max(s))

questions.stem: Which of the following describes all real solutions of the inequality |x − 6| < 4 ?
questions.explanation: An absolute value less than a positive number gives a single "between" interval: −4 < x − 6 < 4. Adding 6 throughout gives 2 < x < 10. The "or" choices belong to a > inequality, not a < inequality.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes all real solutions of the inequality |2x + 1| ≥ 9 ?
questions.explanation: An absolute value greater than or equal to a positive number splits into two branches: 2x + 1 ≥ 9 gives x ≥ 4, and 2x + 1 ≤ −9 gives x ≤ −5. So the solution is x ≤ −5 or x ≥ 4. The "between" choices reverse the direction of the inequality.

questions.stem: What is the solution set of the equation 3|x − 2| + 5 = 17 ?
questions.explanation: Isolate the absolute value first: 3|x − 2| = 12, so |x − 2| = 4. Then x − 2 = 4 gives x = 6 and x − 2 = −4 gives x = −2. Choice {−10, 14} comes from forgetting to divide by 3, and {6} keeps only the positive branch.
questions.verify:
sols=sorted(x for x in range(-100,101) if 3*abs(x-2)+5==17)
"{"+", ".join(str(s).replace("-","−") for s in sols)+"}"

questions.stem: How many real solutions does the equation |4x − 3| + 9 = 2 have?
questions.explanation: Isolating the absolute value gives |4x − 3| = −7. An absolute value is never negative, so no real value of x works. Solving the two cases anyway produces values that fail when checked in the original equation.
questions.verify: "None" if all(abs(4*(x/100)-3)+9!=2 for x in range(-20000,20001)) else "Some"

questions.stem: A bottling machine is set to put 500 milliliters of juice into each bottle. A bottle passes inspection only if its actual volume v, in milliliters, differs from 500 milliliters by no more than 12 milliliters. Which of the following inequalities describes exactly the volumes that pass inspection?
questions.explanation: "Differs from 500 by no more than 12" means the distance between v and 500 is at most 12, which is written |v − 500| ≤ 12. This unpacks to 488 ≤ v ≤ 512. The ≥ version describes the bottles that fail, and swapping 12 and 500 measures distance from the wrong center.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes all real solutions of the inequality |5 − 2x| ≤ 7 ?
questions.explanation: Write the compound inequality −7 ≤ 5 − 2x ≤ 7, then subtract 5 to get −12 ≤ −2x ≤ 2. Dividing by −2 reverses both inequality signs, giving 6 ≥ x ≥ −1, that is, −1 ≤ x ≤ 6. Choice −6 ≤ x ≤ 1 comes from dividing by −2 without reversing the signs.
questions.verify:
xs=[i/100 for i in range(-1000,1001)]
ok=[x for x in xs if abs(5-2*x)<=7]
f"{min(ok):g} ≤ x ≤ {max(ok):g}".replace("-","−")

questions.stem: What are all the real solutions of the equation |x + 5| = 3x − 1 ?
questions.explanation: Case 1: x + 5 = 3x − 1 gives 2x = 6, so x = 3, and checking gives |8| = 8 = 3(3) − 1. Case 2: x + 5 = −(3x − 1) gives 4x = −4, so x = −1, but then |4| = 4 while 3(−1) − 1 = −4, so it is extraneous. Only x = 3 works.
questions.verify:
from fractions import Fraction
sols=[Fraction(n,4) for n in range(-200,201) if abs(Fraction(n,4)+5)==3*Fraction(n,4)-1]
f"x = {sols[0]} only" if len(sols)==1 else str(sols)

questions.stem: The solution set of the inequality |x + a| < 5 is −8 < x < 2. What is the value of a ?
questions.explanation: The inequality unpacks to −5 < x + a < 5, so −5 − a < x < 5 − a. Matching endpoints, 5 − a = 2 and −5 − a = −8 both give a = 3. Choice −3 comes from matching the center of the interval, −3, to a directly.

questions.stem: Lines ℓ and m are parallel and are cut by a transversal. One of the angles formed measures 72°, and the corresponding angle at the other line measures (3x)°. What is the value of x ?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles formed by a transversal cutting parallel lines are congruent, so 3x = 72 and x = 24. Choice 36 comes from treating the angles as supplementary (3x = 108), and 72 and 108 forget to divide by 3.

questions.stem: Lines ℓ and m are parallel and are cut by a transversal. Two interior angles that lie on the same side of the transversal measure (2x + 10)° and (4x + 20)°. What is the value of x ?
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles are supplementary, so (2x + 10) + (4x + 20) = 180. That gives 6x + 30 = 180, so x = 25. Choice −5 comes from setting the two expressions equal, and 10 comes from using 90° instead of 180°.

questions.stem: Two straight roads cross at a single point. Two of the angles formed at that intersection are vertical angles whose measures are (5x − 12)° and (3x + 20)°. What is the value of x ?
questions.explanation: Vertical angles are congruent, so 5x − 12 = 3x + 20. Then 2x = 32 and x = 16. Choice 32 stops at 2x = 32, and 21.5 comes from treating the angles as supplementary.

questions.stem: Lines ℓ and m are parallel and are cut by a transversal. A pair of alternate exterior angles measure (7x − 15)° and (5x + 21)°. What is the measure of each of these two angles?
questions.explanation: Alternate exterior angles are congruent, so 7x − 15 = 5x + 21, giving 2x = 36 and x = 18. Substituting back, the measure is 7(18) − 15 = 111°. Choice 18° reports x instead of the angle, and 69° is the supplement of the correct answer.

questions.stem: Two angles are complementary, and one of them is 4 times as large as the other. What is the measure of the smaller angle?
questions.explanation: Let the smaller angle be x°; then the larger is 4x° and x + 4x = 90, so x = 18. The smaller angle measures 18° and the larger measures 72°. Choice 36° uses 180° instead of 90°, and 22.5° divides 90 by 4.
questions.verify:
[a for a in range(1,90) if a+4*a==90][0]
f"{[a for a in range(1,90) if a+4*a==90][0]}°"

questions.stem: Lines ℓ and m are parallel and are cut by a transversal t. One of the acute angles formed measures (4x)° and one of the obtuse angles formed measures (5x + 27)°. What is the value of x ?
questions.explanation: When a transversal cuts parallel lines, every acute angle formed is supplementary to every obtuse angle formed, so 4x + (5x + 27) = 180. Then 9x = 153 and x = 17. Choice 20 comes from forgetting the 27, and 153 stops before dividing by 9.

questions.stem: Ray BD bisects ∠ABC. If m∠ABD = (2x + 5)° and m∠DBC = (4x − 19)°, what is m∠ABC ?
questions.explanation: A bisector creates two congruent angles, so 2x + 5 = 4x − 19, giving 2x = 24 and x = 12. Each half measures 2(12) + 5 = 29°, so the whole angle is 2(29) = 58°. Choice 29° reports only one half, and 12° reports x.

questions.stem: A carpenter makes one straight cut across two parallel boards. The cut forms a pair of alternate interior angles measuring (3x + 5)° and (2x + 25)°. What is the value of x ?
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles at parallel lines are congruent, so 3x + 5 = 2x + 25 and x = 20. Choice 30 comes from setting the sum equal to 180°, and 65 is the measure of each angle rather than the value of x.

questions.stem: Lines ℓ and m are parallel and are cut by a transversal t. The bisectors of the two interior angles on the same side of t are drawn, and they intersect at a point. What is the measure of an angle formed at that point of intersection?
questions.explanation: The two same-side interior angles have measures a° and (180 − a)°. Their bisectors make angles of a/2 and (180 − a)/2 = 90 − a/2 with the transversal, and those two bisectors plus the transversal form a triangle. The remaining angle is 180 − a/2 − (90 − a/2) = 90°, no matter what a is.
questions.verify:
vals={180-(a/2)-(90-a/2) for a in range(20,160)}
f"{int(vals.pop())}°"

questions.stem: Two supplementary angles have measures in the ratio 4:5. What is the measure of the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Let the measures be 4k and 5k. Supplementary means 4k + 5k = 180, so 9k = 180 and k = 20, making the angles 80° and 100°. The larger is 100°. Choices 40° and 50° come from using 90° instead of 180°, and 80° is the smaller angle.

questions.stem: A square has an area of 121 square centimeters. What is the perimeter of the square, in centimeters?
questions.explanation: Each side of the square measures √121 = 11 cm, so the perimeter is 4(11) = 44 cm. Choice 11 is a single side and 22 doubles the side instead of quadrupling it.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has an area of 126 square centimeters and a base of 14 centimeters. What is the height of the parallelogram, in centimeters?
questions.explanation: For a parallelogram, area = base × height, so height = 126 ÷ 14 = 9 cm. Choice 4.5 uses the triangle formula and includes an extra factor of 1/2, and 18 divides by 7 instead of 14.

questions.stem: What is the area, in square inches, of a trapezoid whose parallel sides measure 8 inches and 14 inches and whose height is 6 inches?
questions.explanation: The area of a trapezoid is (1/2)(b₁ + b₂)h = (1/2)(8 + 14)(6) = (1/2)(22)(6) = 66 square inches. Choice 132 forgets the factor of 1/2, and 112 multiplies the two parallel sides together.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 46 inches and a width of 8 inches. What is the area of the rectangle, in square inches?
questions.explanation: From 2(L + 8) = 46 we get L + 8 = 23, so the length is 15 inches and the area is 15 × 8 = 120 square inches. Choice 184 uses the half-perimeter 23 as the length, and 240 uses 46 − 8 − 8 = 30 without halving.

questions.stem: A circle is inscribed in a square whose sides are each 12 centimeters long. What is the area, in square centimeters, of the region that is inside the square but outside the circle?
questions.explanation: The square has area 12² = 144. The inscribed circle has diameter 12, so its radius is 6 and its area is π(6²) = 36π. The remaining region has area 144 − 36π; using radius 12 gives the trap 144 − 144π.

questions.stem: A rectangular garden measures 15 feet by 10 feet. A walkway 2 feet wide is built all the way around the outside of the garden. What is the total area, in square feet, of the garden and walkway together?
questions.explanation: The walkway adds 2 feet on each of the two opposite sides, so the outer rectangle is 15 + 4 = 19 feet by 10 + 4 = 14 feet, giving 19 × 14 = 266 square feet. Choice 210 adds the walkway to only one dimension: 15 × (10 + 4). Choice 150 is the garden alone, and 116 is the area of the walkway alone.

questions.stem: A rectangular dog run measures 18 feet by 24 feet. Fencing costs $7 per foot. What is the total cost of fencing all four sides of the dog run?
questions.explanation: The perimeter is 2(18 + 24) = 84 feet, so the cost is 84 × $7 = $588. Choice $294 fences only two sides, and $3,024 multiplies the area 432 square feet by $7.

questions.stem: A triangle has an area of 84 square centimeters and a height of 7 centimeters. What is the length of the base, in centimeters?
questions.explanation: From area = (1/2)bh, we get 84 = (1/2)b(7), so 3.5b = 84 and b = 24 cm. Choice 12 divides 84 by 7 and forgets to undo the factor of 1/2, and 42 is half of 84.

questions.stem: If the length of each side of a square is increased by 50%, by what percent is the area of the square increased?
questions.explanation: If the original side is s, the new side is 1.5s and the new area is (1.5s)² = 2.25s². That is an increase of 1.25s², or 125% of the original area. Choice 50% applies the side's percent increase directly to the area, and 100% assumes the area doubles.

questions.stem: The diagonals of a rhombus measure 16 centimeters and 30 centimeters. What is the perimeter of the rhombus, in centimeters?
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, forming right triangles with legs 8 and 15, so each side is √(8² + 15²) = 17 cm. The perimeter is 4(17) = 68 cm. Choice 240 is the area, and 92 adds the diagonals as if they were side lengths.

questions.stem: A rectangular tabletop measures 30 inches by 48 inches. What is the area of the tabletop, in square inches?
questions.explanation: The area of a rectangle is length × width = 30 × 48 = 1,440 square inches. Choice 156 is the perimeter, 78 is half the perimeter, and 720 halves the area as if the tabletop were a triangle.

questions.stem: A triangular sign has sides measuring 7.5 centimeters, 9.25 centimeters, and 12 centimeters. What is the perimeter of the sign, in centimeters?
questions.explanation: Perimeter is the sum of all three sides: 7.5 + 9.25 + 12 = 28.75 centimeters. Choice 21.25 leaves out one side, and 57.5 doubles the perimeter.

questions.stem: A cube has a volume of 216 cubic centimeters. What is the length, in centimeters, of one edge of the cube?
questions.explanation: For a cube, V = e³, so e = ∛216 = 6 centimeters. Choice 72 comes from dividing 216 by 3 instead of taking a cube root, and 36 is the area of one face.

questions.stem: A rectangular room measures 15 feet by 12 feet. Carpet costs $28 per square yard. What is the cost of enough carpet to cover the entire floor? (1 square yard = 9 square feet)
questions.explanation: The floor is 15 × 12 = 180 square feet, which is 180 ÷ 9 = 20 square yards. The cost is 20 × $28 = $560. Choice $5,040 skips the unit conversion, and $1,680 divides by 3 instead of 9.

questions.stem: A circular tablecloth has a diameter of 5 feet. What is the area of the tablecloth, to the nearest tenth of a square foot?
questions.explanation: The radius is 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5 feet, so the area is π(2.5)² ≈ 19.6 square feet. Choice 78.5 uses the diameter as the radius, and 15.7 is the circumference rather than the area.

questions.stem: A rectangular swimming pool is 20 feet long, 12 feet wide, and 5 feet deep. If 1 cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons, about how many gallons of water does the full pool hold?
questions.explanation: The volume is 20 × 12 × 5 = 1,200 cubic feet, and 1,200 × 7.5 = 9,000 gallons. Choice 1,200 stops at cubic feet, and 160 divides by 7.5 instead of multiplying.

questions.stem: A rectangular sheet of poster board measures 24 inches by 36 inches. It is cut, with no waste, into squares that each measure 6 inches on a side. How many such squares are produced?
questions.explanation: The sheet fits 24 ÷ 6 = 4 squares along one side and 36 ÷ 6 = 6 along the other, so there are 4 × 6 = 24 squares. Choice 864 is the total area in square inches, and 144 divides that area by 6 instead of by 36, the area of one square.

questions.stem: A rectangular garden measures 20 feet by 14 feet. A path of uniform width 3 feet is built around the outside of the garden. What is the area of the path alone, in square feet?
questions.explanation: The outer rectangle measures 20 + 6 = 26 feet by 14 + 6 = 20 feet, with area 520 square feet; the garden itself is 280 square feet, so the path is 520 − 280 = 240 square feet. Choice 111 adds only 3 feet to each dimension, and 204 = 2(3)(20 + 14) ignores the four corner squares.

questions.stem: On a scale drawing of a room, 1 inch represents 4 feet. The room appears on the drawing as a rectangle measuring 3.5 inches by 5 inches. What is the actual area of the room, in square feet?
questions.explanation: The actual dimensions are 3.5 × 4 = 14 feet and 5 × 4 = 20 feet, so the area is 14 × 20 = 280 square feet. Choice 70 multiplies the drawing's area by 4 only once; because area scales by the square of the ratio, the factor is 4² = 16.

questions.stem: A cylindrical tank with a radius of 3 feet and a height of 8 feet is empty. Water is pumped in at a constant rate of 6 cubic feet per minute. To the nearest minute, how long does it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: The volume is πr²h = π(3²)(8) = 72π ≈ 226.2 cubic feet, and 226.2 ÷ 6 ≈ 37.7, so it takes about 38 minutes. Choice 226 is the volume itself, and 12 drops the factor of π.

questions.stem: A circle has a diameter of 18 centimeters. What is the circumference of the circle, in centimeters?
questions.explanation: The circumference is C = πd = 18π centimeters. Choice 36π treats 18 as the radius in C = 2πr, while 81π is the area and 324π uses πd².

questions.stem: A circle has an area of 49π square inches. What is the diameter of the circle, in inches?
questions.explanation: From πr² = 49π we get r² = 49, so r = 7 and the diameter is 2(7) = 14 inches. Choice 7 gives the radius rather than the diameter, and 49 forgets the square root entirely.

questions.stem: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, which of the following is an equation of the circle with center (−3, 5) and radius 6 ?
questions.explanation: The circle with center (h,k) and radius r has equation (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r². With h = −3 and k = 5 the binomials are (x + 3) and (y − 5), and r² = 36. Choices with "= 6" forget to square the radius, and the sign-flipped versions use the coordinates instead of their opposites.

questions.stem: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, a circle has equation (x − 2)² + (y + 7)² = 45. What is the radius of this circle?
questions.explanation: The right side equals r², so r = √45 = √(9 · 5) = 3√5. Choice 45 forgets the square root, 22.5 halves it instead, and 5√3 factors 45 incorrectly (5√3 = √75).
questions.verify:
n=45
k=max(i for i in range(1,10) if n%(i*i)==0)
f"{k}√{n//(k*k)}"

questions.stem: In a circle of radius 12 inches, a central angle intercepts a minor arc of length 5π inches. What is the measure of that central angle?
questions.explanation: Arc length is (θ/360) · 2πr = (θ/360)(24π). Setting this equal to 5π gives θ/360 = 5/24, so θ = 75°. Choice 150° uses the radius in place of the diameter in the circumference, and 37.5° halves the correct answer.

questions.stem: Two concentric circles have radii of 5 meters and 8 meters. What is the area, in square meters, of the ring-shaped region between them?
questions.explanation: Subtract the areas: π(8²) − π(5²) = 64π − 25π = 39π square meters. Choice 64π forgets to remove the inner circle, 89π adds the areas, and 169π squares the sum of the radii.

questions.stem: A chord of a circle is 16 centimeters long, and the distance from the center of the circle to the chord is 6 centimeters. What is the radius of the circle, in centimeters?
questions.explanation: The perpendicular segment from the center bisects the chord, forming a right triangle with legs 8 and 6 and hypotenuse r. So r = √(8² + 6²) = √100 = 10 centimeters. Choice 8 is half the chord, and 14 adds the two legs instead of using the Pythagorean theorem.

questions.stem: A circle is inscribed in a square whose perimeter is 40 inches. What is the area of the circle, in square inches?
questions.explanation: Each side of the square is 40 ÷ 4 = 10 inches, and the inscribed circle has diameter 10, so its radius is 5. The area is π(5²) = 25π square inches. Choice 100π uses the diameter as the radius, and 10π is the circumference.

questions.stem: A sector of a circle has a central angle of 135° and an area of 24π square centimeters. What is the radius of the circle, in centimeters?
questions.explanation: Sector area is (135/360)πr² = (3/8)πr². Setting (3/8)πr² = 24π gives r² = 64, so r = 8 centimeters. Choice 2√6 = √24 ignores the fraction of the circle, and 4√2 comes from using 135/180 instead of 135/360.

questions.stem: A bicycle wheel has a diameter of 26 inches. How many complete revolutions does the wheel make while the bicycle travels 1 mile? (1 mile = 63,360 inches)
questions.explanation: One revolution covers the circumference, π(26) ≈ 81.68 inches, and 63,360 ÷ 81.68 ≈ 775.7, so the wheel completes 775 full revolutions. Choice 2,436 divides by 26 without using π, and 387 treats 26 as the radius.

questions.stem: For i = √(−1), what is the sum (4 + 7i) + (5 − 2i) ?
questions.explanation: Add real parts and imaginary parts separately: (4 + 5) + (7 − 2)i = 9 + 5i. Choice 9 + 9i adds the imaginary parts as if both were positive, and 9 − 5i flips the sign of the imaginary part.

questions.stem: Two circuit components connected in series have a combined impedance of (10 − 2i) ohms. One of the components has impedance (6 + 3i) ohms. What is the impedance, in ohms, of the other component?
questions.explanation: In series the impedances add, so the unknown impedance is (10 − 2i) − (6 + 3i) = (10 − 6) + (−2 − 3)i = 4 − 5i ohms. Choice 4 + i adds the imaginary parts instead of subtracting them; choice 4 + 5i subtracts them in the wrong order, 3 − (−2); and choice 16 + i adds both components instead of subtracting.
Write each radical in terms of i: √(−49) = 7i and √(−16) = 4i, so the sum is 11i. Choice 11 drops the i, and i√65 comes from incorrectly combining the two radicands under one radical.

questions.stem: For i = √(−1), what is the value of i⁴⁵ ?
questions.explanation: Powers of i repeat in a cycle of 4. Since 45 = 4(11) + 1, i⁴⁵ = (i⁴)¹¹ · i¹ = 1 · i = i. Reading the remainder as 0, 2, or 3 gives the traps 1, −1, and −i.

questions.stem: For i = √(−1), what is the product (2 + 5i)(2 − 5i) ?
questions.explanation: These are complex conjugates, so the product is 2² − (5i)² = 4 − 25i² = 4 + 25 = 29. Choice −21 uses i² = +1 instead of −1, and the choices with an i term never square the imaginary unit.

questions.stem: The expression 5i(4 − 3i) is equivalent to which of the following, where i² = −1 ?
questions.explanation: Distribute the monomial: 5i(4) − 5i(3i) = 20i − 15i². Since i² = −1, the second term becomes +15, so the result is 15 + 20i. Choice −15 + 20i treats i² as +1, and 20i drops the second term entirely.

questions.stem: For i = √(−1), which of the following is equal to (4 + 2i)/(1 + i) ?
questions.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate 1 − i: the denominator becomes 1² + 1² = 2 and the numerator becomes 4 − 4i + 2i − 2i² = 6 − 2i. Dividing by 2 gives 3 − i. Choice 6 − 2i forgets to divide by 2, and 3 + i uses the wrong conjugate sign.
questions.verify:
z=complex(4,2)/complex(1,1)
a=int(round(z.real))
b=int(round(z.imag))
f"{a} − i" if b==-1 else "?"

questions.stem: What are the solutions of the equation x² + 4x + 13 = 0 ?
questions.explanation: By the quadratic formula, x = (−4 ± √(16 − 52))/2 = (−4 ± √(−36))/2 = (−4 ± 6i)/2 = −2 ± 3i. Choice −4 ± 6i skips the division by 2, and 2 ± 3i drops the negative sign on −b.
questions.verify:
import cmath
r=(-4+cmath.sqrt(16-4*13))/2
a=int(round(r.real))
b=int(round(abs(r.imag)))
f"{a} ± {b}i".replace("-","−")

questions.stem: The real numbers a and b satisfy (a + bi)(2 − i) = 7 + 4i, where i = √(−1). What is the value of a + b ?
questions.explanation: Divide: a + bi = (7 + 4i)/(2 − i) = (7 + 4i)(2 + i)/5 = (14 + 7i + 8i − 4)/5 = (10 + 15i)/5 = 2 + 3i. So a = 2, b = 3, and a + b = 5. Choice 11 adds the real and imaginary parts of 7 + 4i instead.

questions.stem: For i = √(−1), what is the value of i + i² + i³ + … + i⁵⁰ ?
questions.explanation: Any four consecutive powers of i sum to i + (−1) + (−i) + 1 = 0. Since 50 = 4(12) + 2, the first 48 terms cancel and only i⁴⁹ + i⁵⁰ = i + i² = i − 1 remains, which is −1 + i. Choice 0 assumes all 50 terms pair off.
questions.verify:
s=sum(1j**k for k in range(1,51))
a=int(round(s.real))
b=int(round(s.imag))
(f"{a} + i".replace("-","−") if b==1 else "?")

questions.stem: A bag contains 5 red marbles and 7 blue marbles. One marble is drawn at random and is red; it is NOT put back. What is the probability that a second marble drawn at random is also red?
questions.explanation: After the first red marble is removed, 4 red marbles remain out of 11 total, so the probability is 4/11. Choice 5/12 ignores the first draw, and 4/12 reduces the reds without reducing the total.
questions.verify:
from fractions import Fraction
f=Fraction(5-1,12-1)
f"{f.numerator}/{f.denominator}"

questions.stem: One card is drawn at random from a standard 52-card deck. Given that the card drawn is a face card (jack, queen, or king), what is the probability that it is a king?
questions.explanation: Conditioning on face cards shrinks the sample space to the 12 face cards, of which 4 are kings, so the probability is 4/12 = 1/3. Choice 1/13 is the unconditional probability of a king, and 3/13 is the probability of drawing a face card.
questions.verify:
from fractions import Fraction
f=Fraction(4,12)
f"{f.numerator}/{f.denominator}"

questions.stem:
The table below shows the members of a school club, classified by grade level and by whether they went on a field trip.

Grade | Went | Did not go
Junior | 24 | 16
Senior | 30 | 10

Given that a randomly selected club member went on the field trip, what is the probability that the member is a junior?
questions.explanation: Conditioning on "went on the trip" restricts attention to the 24 + 30 = 54 members who went, of whom 24 are juniors, giving 24/54 = 4/9. Choice 3/5 is the probability a junior went (24/40), reversing the condition, and 3/10 is the unconditional joint probability 24/80.
questions.verify:
from fractions import Fraction
f=Fraction(24,24+30)
f"{f.numerator}/{f.denominator}"

questions.stem: A fair 6-sided die with faces numbered 1 through 6 is rolled once. Given that the result is an even number, what is the probability that the result is greater than 3 ?
questions.explanation: The condition restricts the outcomes to {2, 4, 6}, and two of those three outcomes exceed 3, so the probability is 2/3. Choice 1/3 is P(even and greater than 3) = 2/6, and 1/2 is the unconditional probability of a result greater than 3.
questions.verify:
from fractions import Fraction
ev=[n for n in range(1,7) if n%2==0]
f=Fraction(len([n for n in ev if n>3]),len(ev))
f"{f.numerator}/{f.denominator}"

questions.stem: In a class of 30 students, 18 play a sport, 12 play a musical instrument, and 7 do both. If a student who plays a sport is selected at random, what is the probability that the student also plays an instrument?
questions.explanation: The condition limits the group to the 18 students who play a sport, and 7 of them also play an instrument, so the probability is 7/18. Choice 7/12 reverses the condition, and 7/30 uses the whole class as the denominator.
questions.verify:
from fractions import Fraction
f=Fraction(7,18)
f"{f.numerator}/{f.denominator}"

questions.stem: A jar contains 6 green marbles and 4 yellow marbles. Two marbles are drawn at random, one after the other, without replacement. What is the probability that both marbles are green?
questions.explanation: P(first green) = 6/10, and given that, P(second green) = 5/9, so the probability of both is (6/10)(5/9) = 30/90 = 1/3. Choice 9/25 uses (6/10)², which would be correct only with replacement, and 3/5 is just the first draw.
questions.verify:
from fractions import Fraction
f=Fraction(6,10)*Fraction(5,9)
f"{f.numerator}/{f.denominator}"

questions.stem:
A survey of 150 commuters recorded whether each takes the bus and whether each owns a car.

Group | Owns a car | Does not own a car
Takes the bus | 27 | 45
Does not take the bus | 63 | 15

Given that a randomly selected commuter takes the bus, what is the probability that the commuter owns a car?
questions.explanation: The 72 bus riders form the reduced sample space, and 27 of them own a car, so the probability is 27/72 = 3/8. Choice 3/10 is P(takes the bus | owns a car) = 27/90, and 9/50 is the joint probability 27/150.
questions.verify:

f=Fraction(27,27+45)

questions.stem: For two events A and B, P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.5, and P(A and B) = 0.3. What is P(A | B) ?
questions.explanation: By definition, P(A | B) = P(A and B)/P(B) = 0.3/0.5 = 0.6. Choice 0.5 divides by P(A) instead, giving P(B | A), and 0.15 multiplies the probabilities rather than dividing.

questions.stem: A company makes widgets at two plants. Plant A produces 70% of the widgets, and 2% of those are defective. Plant B produces the other 30%, and 5% of those are defective. Given that a randomly chosen widget is defective, what is the probability that it came from Plant A?
questions.explanation: P(A and defective) = 0.70(0.02) = 0.014 and P(B and defective) = 0.30(0.05) = 0.015, so P(defective) = 0.029. Then P(A | defective) = 0.014/0.029 = 14/29. Choice 15/29 is the probability the defective widget came from Plant B, and 7/10 ignores the defect information.
questions.verify:

f=Fraction(70*2,70*2+30*5)
f"{f.numerator}/{f.denominator}"

questions.stem: A box contains 3 fair coins and 1 two-headed coin. One coin is selected at random and flipped once, and it lands heads up. What is the probability that the coin selected was the two-headed coin?
questions.explanation: P(two-headed and heads) = (1/4)(1) = 1/4, and P(fair and heads) = (3/4)(1/2) = 3/8, so P(heads) = 1/4 + 3/8 = 5/8. The conditional probability is (1/4)/(5/8) = 2/5. Choice 1/4 is the prior probability, before the flip is observed.

questions.stem: In the standard (x, y) coordinate plane, what is the midpoint of the line segment with endpoints (2, −3) and (8, 5)?
questions.explanation: The midpoint averages the coordinates: ((2 + 8)/2, (−3 + 5)/2) = (5, 1). Choice (3, 4) halves the coordinate differences instead of averaging, and (10, 2) adds the coordinates without dividing by 2.

questions.stem: What is the slope of the line that passes through the points (−3, 7) and (5, −9) in the standard (x, y) coordinate plane?
questions.explanation: Slope is the change in y over the change in x: (−9 − 7)/(5 − (−3)) = −16/8 = −2. Choice 2 drops the negative sign, and −1/2 inverts rise over run.

questions.stem: On a city map in the standard (x, y) coordinate plane, each grid unit represents 1 kilometer. A delivery drone flies in a straight line from a warehouse at (2, −1) to a stadium at (7, 11). How many kilometers long is the drone's flight?
questions.explanation: By the distance formula, d = √((7 − 2)² + (11 − (−1))²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13 kilometers. Choice 17 adds the legs 5 and 12 instead of using the Pythagorean relationship, and 169 forgets to take the square root.

questions.stem: A circle in the standard (x, y) coordinate plane has the equation x² + y² + 10x − 4y + 20 = 0. What is the x-coordinate of the center of the circle?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: (x² + 10x + 25) + (y² − 4y + 4) = −20 + 25 + 4, so (x + 5)² + (y − 2)² = 9. The center is (−5, 2), so the x-coordinate is −5. Choice 5 uses the wrong sign, since (x + 5)² means x = −5.

questions.stem: In the standard (x, y) coordinate plane, what is the slope of any line perpendicular to the line 3x − 4y = 8?
questions.explanation: Solving 3x − 4y = 8 for y gives y = (3/4)x − 2, so the line has slope 3/4. A perpendicular line has the opposite reciprocal slope, −4/3. Choice 3/4 is the slope of the given line itself, and −3/4 changes the sign without taking the reciprocal.

questions.stem: In the standard (x, y) coordinate plane, a line passes through the point (2, 5) and is parallel to the line y = 3x − 4. What is the y-intercept of this line?
questions.explanation: A parallel line has the same slope, 3, so the line is y = 3x + b. Substituting (2, 5) gives 5 = 3(2) + b, so b = −1. Choice 11 adds 3(2) to 5 instead of subtracting.

questions.stem: In the standard (x, y) coordinate plane, the points (−2, 3) and (6, −3) are the endpoints of a diameter of a circle. Which of the following is an equation of the circle?
questions.explanation: The center is the midpoint of the diameter, ((−2 + 6)/2, (3 + (−3))/2) = (2, 0). The diameter is √(8² + 6²) = 10, so the radius is 5 and r² = 25, giving (x − 2)² + y² = 25. The choice with 100 uses the diameter squared, and the choice with 5 uses the radius instead of the radius squared.

questions.stem: In the standard (x, y) coordinate plane, a triangle has vertices (0, 0), (8, 0), and (3, 6). What is the area, in square coordinate units, of the triangle?
questions.explanation: The side from (0, 0) to (8, 0) lies on the x-axis, so it is a base of length 8. The height is the y-coordinate of (3, 6), which is 6. Area = (1/2)(8)(6) = 24 square units; choice 48 forgets the factor of 1/2.

questions.stem: In the standard (x, y) coordinate plane, what is the distance from the point (3, −1) to the line 4x − 3y + 5 = 0?
questions.explanation: The distance from (x₀, y₀) to ax + by + c = 0 is |ax₀ + by₀ + c|/√(a² + b²). Here that is |4(3) − 3(−1) + 5|/√(16 + 9) = 20/5 = 4. Choice 20 is the numerator alone, and 5 is the denominator √25.

questions.stem: In the standard (x, y) coordinate plane, the points (−2, k) and (4, 1) lie on a line with slope 3/2. What is the value of k?
questions.explanation: The slope condition gives (1 − k)/(4 − (−2)) = 3/2, so 1 − k = (3/2)(6) = 9 and k = −8. Choice 10 comes from writing k − 1 = 9, a sign error in the slope ratio, and −2 uses a run of 2 instead of 6.

questions.stem: A food truck makes each taco with exactly 1 of 3 shell types and exactly 1 of 4 salsas. How many different tacos are possible?
questions.explanation: By the fundamental counting principle, multiply the number of independent choices: 3 × 4 = 12. Choice 7 adds the options instead of multiplying, and 81 computes 3⁴.

questions.stem: In how many different orders can 5 students stand in a single line for a photograph?
questions.explanation: There are 5 choices for the first position, 4 for the second, and so on: 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120. Choice 25 computes 5², and 20 stops after 5 × 4.

questions.stem: Eight sprinters compete in a race in which gold, silver, and bronze medals are awarded to the top 3 finishers. In how many different ways can the 3 medals be awarded?
questions.explanation: Order matters, so this is a permutation: 8 choices for gold, 7 for silver, 6 for bronze, giving 8 × 7 × 6 = 336. Choice 56 is the combination 8C3, which ignores order, and 512 is 8³, which allows repeated winners.

questions.stem: A principal will choose 3 of the school's 7 teachers to serve on a committee. How many different committees of 3 teachers are possible?
questions.explanation: Order does not matter on a committee, so use combinations: 7C3 = (7 × 6 × 5)/(3 × 2 × 1) = 35. Choice 210 is the permutation 7 × 6 × 5, which counts each committee 6 times, and 343 is 7³.

questions.stem: A gym assigns each member a 4-digit locker code using the digits 0 through 9. No digit may be repeated, and the first digit cannot be 0. How many different locker codes are possible?
questions.explanation: The first digit has 9 options (1–9). The second digit can be any unused digit including 0, so it also has 9 options, then 8 and 7 remain: 9 × 9 × 8 × 7 = 4,536. Choice 5,040 ignores the leading-zero restriction, and 10,000 allows repeats and leading zeros.

questions.stem: How many distinct arrangements can be made using all 5 letters of the word LEVEL?
questions.explanation: There are 5! = 120 arrangements of 5 letters, but the two L's are identical and the two E's are identical. Divide by 2! for each repeated letter: 120/(2! × 2!) = 30. Choice 120 ignores the repeats, and 60 divides by only one 2!.

questions.stem: In a school play, 3 boys and 3 girls will sit in a row of 6 chairs so that boys and girls alternate seats. How many such seating arrangements are possible?
questions.explanation: The pattern is either boy-first or girl-first: 2 options. For each pattern, the 3 boys can fill their seats in 3! = 6 ways and the girls in 3! = 6 ways. Total: 2 × 6 × 6 = 72; choice 36 forgets the 2 possible patterns, and 720 is 6! with no alternating restriction.

questions.stem: A caterer will select 2 different appetizers from a list of 6 and 1 main dish from a list of 5. How many different selections of 2 appetizers and 1 main dish are possible?
questions.explanation: The 2 appetizers are an unordered pair: 6C2 = 15 choices. Multiply by the 5 main dishes: 15 × 5 = 75. Choice 150 counts the appetizers in order (6 × 5 × 5), and 30 pairs each of the 6 appetizers with a main dish, choosing only 1 appetizer.

questions.stem: Four different math books and 2 different art books will be arranged on a shelf so that the 2 art books are next to each other. How many such arrangements are possible?
questions.explanation: Treat the 2 art books as a single block, giving 5 objects to arrange in 5! = 120 ways. The art books can be ordered within the block in 2! = 2 ways, so there are 120 × 2 = 240 arrangements. Choice 720 is 6! with no restriction, and 120 forgets to order the art books within the block.

questions.stem: In a soccer league, each pair of teams plays exactly 2 games against each other, one at each team's home field. A total of 90 games are played. How many teams are in the league?
questions.explanation: With n teams, each of the n(n − 1)/2 pairs plays 2 games, so n(n − 1) = 90. Since 10 × 9 = 90, there are 10 teams. Choice 45 is the number of pairs of teams, not the number of teams.
questions.verify: next(n for n in range(2,50) if n*(n-1)==90)

questions.stem: A fair spinner has 4 equal sectors labeled 2, 4, 6, and 8. What is the expected value of the number the spinner lands on for one spin?
questions.explanation: Each sector has probability 1/4, so the expected value is (2)(1/4) + (4)(1/4) + (6)(1/4) + (8)(1/4) = 20/4 = 5. Choice 20 is the sum of the labels without dividing by the number of sectors, and 6 is simply one of the labels rather than the mean.

questions.stem: A random variable X takes the values 0, 1, 2, and 3 with probabilities 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 0.1, respectively. What is the expected value of X?
questions.explanation: Multiply each value by its probability and add: 0(0.2) + 1(0.3) + 2(0.4) + 3(0.1) = 0 + 0.3 + 0.8 + 0.3 = 1.4. Choice 1.5 is the unweighted average of 0, 1, 2, 3, and 2 is merely the most likely value.

questions.stem: In a game, a player wins $12 with probability 1/4 and loses $4 otherwise. What is the expected value, in dollars, of the game for one play?
questions.explanation: The loss occurs with probability 3/4, so the expected value is 12(1/4) − 4(3/4) = 3 − 3 = 0. Choice 3 counts only the expected winnings, and 8 simply subtracts 4 from 12.

questions.stem: A player pays $2 to roll a fair 6-sided die once, winning $6 for rolling a 6, winning $3 for rolling a 5, and winning nothing otherwise. What is the player's expected net result, in dollars, for one play?
questions.explanation: The expected prize is 6(1/6) + 3(1/6) = 1.50 dollars. Subtracting the $2 cost gives an expected net result of 1.50 − 2 = −0.50 dollars. Choice 1.50 forgets the cost to play.

questions.stem: An insurance company sells a 1-year policy for $150. The company estimates a 0.01 probability that it will pay out a $10,000 claim on the policy, and no other payouts are possible. What is the company's expected profit, in dollars, on one policy?
questions.explanation: The expected claim payout is 0.01 × 10,000 = 100 dollars. The company collects $150, so its expected profit is 150 − 100 = 50 dollars. Choice 100 is the expected payout itself, and −50 reverses the subtraction.

questions.stem: A student randomly guesses on each of 20 multiple-choice questions. Each question has 4 answer choices, exactly 1 of which is correct. What is the expected number of questions the student answers correctly?
questions.explanation: Each guess is correct with probability 1/4, so the expected number correct is 20 × 1/4 = 5. Choice 10 uses probability 1/2, and 15 uses 3/4, the probability of guessing incorrectly.

questions.stem: For a school fundraiser, exactly 500 raffle tickets are sold at $2 each. One ticket wins a $300 prize, and 5 other tickets each win a $20 prize. What is the expected net value, in dollars, of buying one ticket?
questions.explanation: The total prize money is 300 + 5(20) = 400 dollars, so a ticket's expected prize is 400/500 = 0.80 dollars. Subtracting the $2 cost gives 0.80 − 2 = −1.20 dollars. Choice 0.80 ignores the ticket price, and 1.20 drops the negative sign.

questions.stem: In a game, a player wins $8 with probability p and loses $2 with probability 1 − p. For what value of p is the expected value of the game equal to $0?
questions.explanation: Set the expected value equal to 0: 8p − 2(1 − p) = 0, so 8p − 2 + 2p = 0, giving 10p = 2 and p = 1/5. Choice 1/4 comes from dropping the +2p term and solving 8p = 2, and choice 4/5 reverses the two payoffs by solving 2p = 8(1 − p).

questions.stem: A random variable takes the value 0 with probability 0.5, the value 2 with probability p, and the value 6 with probability 0.5 − p. If the expected value of the random variable is 2, what is the value of p?
questions.explanation: The expected value is 0(0.5) + 2p + 6(0.5 − p) = 3 − 4p. Setting 3 − 4p = 2 gives 4p = 1, so p = 1/4. Choice 1/2 exceeds the total probability available to the values 2 and 6.

questions.stem: Two evenly matched teams play a series that ends as soon as one team has won 2 games, and each team is equally likely to win each game. What is the expected number of games in the series?
questions.explanation: The series lasts 2 games when one team wins the first two, which has probability (1/2)(1/2) + (1/2)(1/2) = 1/2; otherwise it lasts 3 games. The expected length is 2(1/2) + 3(1/2) = 2.5 games. Choice 3 assumes the maximum length is always played.

questions.stem: What is the value of 2⁻³?
questions.explanation: A negative exponent means reciprocal: 2⁻³ = 1/2³ = 1/8. Choice −8 treats the negative exponent as a negative result, and −6 multiplies 2 by −3.

questions.stem: For all x ≠ 0, the expression x⁵ · x⁻² is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: When multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents: 5 + (−2) = 3, so x⁵ · x⁻² = x³. Choice x⁻¹⁰ multiplies the exponents, and x⁷ adds 5 and 2 while ignoring the sign.

questions.stem: What is the value of (2³)⁴ / 2¹⁰?
questions.explanation: A power of a power multiplies exponents: (2³)⁴ = 2¹². Dividing powers subtracts exponents: 2¹²/2¹⁰ = 2² = 4. Choice 1/8 adds 3 and 4 to get 2⁷/2¹⁰ = 2⁻³.

questions.stem: For all x ≠ 0, the expression (4x⁻³)/(2x²) is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: Divide the coefficients: 4/2 = 2. Subtract the exponents: −3 − 2 = −5, so the expression equals 2x⁻⁵ = 2/x⁵. Choice 2x⁵ drops the negative sign, and 2/x adds the exponents to get −3 + 2 = −1.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, simplify
x = symbols("x", positive=True)
expr = (4*x**-3) / (2*x**2)
c = {"2x⁵": 2*x**5, "2/x⁵": 2/x**5, "2/x": 2/x, "2/x⁶": 2/x**6}
[k for k, v in c.items() if simplify(v - expr) == 0][0]

questions.stem: What is the value of 16^(3/4)?
questions.explanation: A fractional exponent means a root and a power: 16^(3/4) = (16^(1/4))³ = 2³ = 8. Choice 12 multiplies 16 by 3/4, choice 2 is only the fourth root, and 64 uses the exponent 3/2 instead of 3/4.

questions.stem: If 5^(2x) = 5⁷ · 5³, then x = ?
questions.explanation: The right side is 5^(7+3) = 5¹⁰. Setting the exponents equal gives 2x = 10, so x = 5. Choice 10 forgets to divide by 2, and 21/2 multiplies the exponents 7 and 3 instead of adding them.
questions.verify:

x = symbols("x")
int(solve(Eq(2*x, 7 + 3), x)[0])

questions.stem: For all nonzero a and b, the expression (3a²b⁻¹)² · (ab³) is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: Square each factor: (3a²b⁻¹)² = 9a⁴b⁻². Multiplying by ab³ adds exponents: 9a⁴⁺¹b⁻²⁺³ = 9a⁵b. Choice 6a⁵b doubles 3 instead of squaring it, and 9a⁵b⁵ treats b⁻² as b².
questions.verify:

a, b = symbols("a b", positive=True)
expr = (3*a**2*b**-1)**2 * (a*b**3)
c = {"9a⁵b": 9*a**5*b, "6a⁵b": 6*a**5*b, "3a⁵b": 3*a**5*b, "9a⁵b⁵": 9*a**5*b**5}
[k for k, v in c.items() if simplify(v - expr) == 0][0]

questions.stem: If 9ˣ · 3^(x+1) = 3⁷, then x = ?
questions.explanation: Rewrite 9 as 3², so 9ˣ = 3^(2x) and the left side becomes 3^(2x) · 3^(x+1) = 3^(3x+1). Setting the exponents equal gives 3x + 1 = 7, so x = 2. Choice 7/3 drops the +1 from the exponent, and 8/3 subtracts 1 instead of adding it when solving.
questions.verify: next(x for x in range(-20,21) if 9**x * 3**(x+1) == 3**7)

questions.stem: For all x > 0, the expression (√x · x^(3/4))/x^(1/4) is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: Write √x as x^(1/2) and combine exponents: 1/2 + 3/4 − 1/4 = 1, so the expression equals x¹ = x. Choice x^(3/2) adds all three exponents without subtracting the denominator's, and x^(3/8) multiplies the fractions.
questions.verify:

e = Fraction(1,2) + Fraction(3,4) - Fraction(1,4)
"x" if e == 1 else "x^(" + str(e) + ")"

questions.stem: If 2ᵃ = 3 and 2ᵇ = 5, what is the value of 2^(2a+b)?
questions.explanation: Split the exponent using the product and power rules: 2^(2a+b) = (2ᵃ)² · 2ᵇ = 3² · 5 = 45. Choice 30 computes 2 · 3 · 5, treating the coefficient 2 as a factor rather than an exponent, and 11 computes 2(3) + 5, adding the powers instead of multiplying them.

questions.stem: A video posted online currently has 500 views, and the number of views is doubling every hour. At this rate, how many views will the video have 3 hours from now?
questions.explanation: Doubling 3 times multiplies the count by 2³ = 8, so the video will have 500 × 8 = 4,000 views. Choice 1,500 multiplies 500 by 3 instead of doubling repeatedly, and 8,000 doubles one extra time.

questions.stem: The value of a car t years after it is purchased is modeled by v(t) = 12,000(0.8)ᵗ dollars. According to the model, what is the value of the car exactly 2 years after purchase?
questions.explanation: Evaluate the model at t = 2: v(2) = 12,000(0.8)² = 12,000(0.64) = 7,680 dollars. Choice $9,600 is the value after only 1 year, and $7,200 subtracts 20% of the original price twice (linear decay).

questions.stem: A gym currently has 350 members, and its membership is expected to increase by 6% per year. Which of the following functions models the number of members M(t) after t years?
questions.explanation: A 6% annual increase multiplies the membership by 1 + 0.06 = 1.06 each year, giving M(t) = 350(1.06)ᵗ. The growth factor must include the original 100%, so 0.06 alone shrinks the count, 1.6 represents 60% growth, and 350 + 0.06t is linear.
questions.verify:
start, pct = 350, 6
def members(t):
    m = start
    for _ in range(t):
        m = m + m * pct / 100
    return m
c = {"M(t) = 350(1.06)ᵗ": lambda t: 350*1.06**t,
     "M(t) = 350(0.06)ᵗ": lambda t: 350*0.06**t,
     "M(t) = 350(1.6)ᵗ": lambda t: 350*1.6**t,
     "M(t) = 350 + 0.06t": lambda t: 350 + 0.06*t}
[k for k, f in c.items() if all(abs(f(t) - members(t)) < 1e-6 for t in range(0, 6))][0]

questions.stem: A laboratory sample contains 80 milligrams of a substance that has a half-life of 6 hours. How many milligrams of the substance will remain after 24 hours?
questions.explanation: In 24 hours there are 24/6 = 4 half-lives, so the amount is multiplied by (1/2)⁴ = 1/16. That leaves 80/16 = 5 milligrams. Choice 10 uses only 3 half-lives, and 40 halves the sample just once.

questions.stem: The number of fish in a pond is modeled by A(t) = 900(0.85)ᵗ, where t is the number of years from now. According to the model, by what percent does the fish population decrease each year?
questions.explanation: The yearly factor 0.85 means the population keeps 85% of its size each year, so it loses 100% − 85% = 15% per year. Choice 85% is the portion that remains, not the decrease.

questions.stem: Marisol deposits $2,000 into an account that earns 3% interest compounded annually, and she makes no other deposits or withdrawals. Which of the following expressions gives the account balance, in dollars, after t years?
questions.explanation: Each year the balance is multiplied by 1 + 0.03 = 1.03, so after t years it is 2,000(1.03)ᵗ. Choice 2,000(1.3)ᵗ uses 30% interest, and 2,000(1 + 0.03t) is simple interest, which grows linearly rather than exponentially.
questions.verify:
start, rate = 2000, 0.03
def bal(t):
    b = start
    for _ in range(t):
        b = b + b * rate
    return b
c = {"2,000(1.3)ᵗ": lambda t: 2000*1.3**t,
     "2,000(1.03)ᵗ": lambda t: 2000*1.03**t,
     "2,000(0.03)ᵗ": lambda t: 2000*0.03**t,
     "2,000(1 + 0.03t)": lambda t: 2000*(1 + 0.03*t)}
[k for k, f in c.items() if all(abs(f(t) - bal(t)) < 1e-6 for t in range(0, 6))][0]

questions.stem: The number of cells in a culture triples every 4 days. The culture currently contains 20 cells. How many cells will the culture contain 12 days from now?
questions.explanation: In 12 days there are 12/4 = 3 tripling periods, so the count is multiplied by 3³ = 27. That gives 20 × 27 = 540 cells. Choice 180 uses only 2 triplings, and 60 triples just once.

questions.stem: For the function f(t) = a · 2ᵗ, where a is a constant, f(3) = 96. What is the value of a?
questions.explanation: Substitute t = 3: a · 2³ = 96, so 8a = 96 and a = 12. Choice 32 divides 96 by 3 instead of by 2³, and 48 divides by 2 only once.
questions.verify:

a = symbols("a")
f = lambda t: a * 2**t
int(solve(Eq(f(3), 96), a)[0])

questions.stem: For the function f(t) = 5 · 2^(t/3), for what value of t does f(t) = 80?
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by 5: 2^(t/3) = 16 = 2⁴. So t/3 = 4 and t = 12. Choice 4 forgets to multiply by 3, and 48 multiplies 16 by 3 instead of the exponent 4.

questions.stem: The value of an investment doubles every 5 years. Which of the following is closest to the percent by which the investment increases each year?
questions.explanation: If r is the annual growth factor, then r⁵ = 2, so r = 2^(1/5) ≈ 1.149, an increase of about 15% per year. Choice 20% divides 100% by 5, ignoring compounding, which would more than double the value in 5 years.

questions.stem: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = x + 5 and g(x) = 3x. What is the value of f(g(2))?
questions.explanation: Work from the inside out: g(2) = 3(2) = 6, and then f(6) = 6 + 5 = 11. Choice 21 computes g(f(2)) instead, and 6 stops after evaluating g(2).

questions.stem: If f(x) = x² and g(x) = 2x − 1, what is the value of f(g(4))?
questions.explanation: Work from the inside out: g(4) = 2(4) − 1 = 7, and then f(7) = 7² = 49. Choice 31 is g(f(4)) = 2(16) − 1, the composition in the wrong order, and 7 stops at g(4).

questions.stem: If f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = √(x − 1), what is the value of g(f(1))?
questions.explanation: First f(1) = 2(1) + 3 = 5, and then g(5) = √(5 − 1) = √4 = 2. Choice 5 stops at f(1), and √5 forgets to subtract 1 inside the radical.

questions.stem: Given f(x) = 3x − 2 and g(x) = x² + 1, which of the following is an expression for f(g(x))?
questions.explanation: Substitute g(x) into f: f(g(x)) = 3(x² + 1) − 2 = 3x² + 3 − 2 = 3x² + 1. Choice 3x² + 3 forgets to subtract 2, and 9x² − 12x + 5 is the reverse composition g(f(x)) = (3x − 2)² + 1.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, expand
x = symbols("x")
f = lambda u: 3*u - 2
g = lambda u: u**2 + 1
truth = expand(f(g(x)))
c = {"3x² + 3": 3*x**2 + 3, "3x² + 1": 3*x**2 + 1,
     "9x² − 12x + 5": 9*x**2 - 12*x + 5, "3x² − 1": 3*x**2 - 1}
[k for k, v in c.items() if expand(v - truth) == 0][0]

questions.stem: If f(x) = 2x − 5, what is the value of f(f(4))?
questions.explanation: First f(4) = 2(4) − 5 = 3, and then f(3) = 2(3) − 5 = 1. Choice 3 applies f only once, and 6 doubles 3 without subtracting 5.

questions.stem: At a shoe store, p(x) = 0.8x gives the price, in dollars, after a 20% discount on an original price of x dollars, and q(x) = x − 10 gives the price after a $10 coupon. What is q(p(50)), the final cost in dollars of a $50 pair of shoes when the discount is applied first and then the coupon?
questions.explanation: First apply the discount: p(50) = 0.8(50) = 40. Then apply the coupon: q(40) = 40 − 10 = 30 dollars. Choice 32 applies the coupon before the discount, p(q(50)) = 0.8(40), and 40 forgets the coupon entirely.

questions.stem: Given f(x) = x + 3 and g(x) = 2x, for what value of x is f(g(x)) = 15?
questions.explanation: The composition is f(g(x)) = 2x + 3. Solving 2x + 3 = 15 gives 2x = 12, so x = 6. Choice 9/2 solves g(f(x)) = 2x + 6 = 15, the reverse order, and 12 stops after subtracting 3.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, Eq, solve
x = symbols("x")
f = lambda u: u + 3
g = lambda u: 2*u
int(solve(Eq(f(g(x)), 15), x)[0])

questions.stem:
The table below gives the values of f(x) and g(x) for x = 1, 2, 3, and 4.

x | f(x) | g(x)
1 | 4 | 2
2 | 3 | 4
3 | 1 | 3
4 | 2 | 1

What is the value of g(f(3))?
questions.explanation: From the table, f(3) = 1. Then read g at that input: g(1) = 2. Choice 1 is f(g(3)) = f(3), the composition in the wrong order, and 3 is g(3) alone.

questions.stem: If f(x) = x² and f(g(x)) = 4x² + 12x + 9 for all x, which of the following could be g(x)?
questions.explanation: Since f squares its input, f(g(x)) = (g(x))². Because 4x² + 12x + 9 = (2x + 3)², one possibility is g(x) = 2x + 3. Choice 2x − 3 squares to 4x² − 12x + 9, which has the wrong middle sign.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, expand
x = symbols("x")
target = 4*x**2 + 12*x + 9
c = {"2x − 3": 2*x - 3, "4x + 3": 4*x + 3, "2x + 9": 2*x + 9, "2x + 3": 2*x + 3}
[k for k, v in c.items() if expand(v**2 - target) == 0][0]

questions.stem: If f(x) = √x and g(x) = x − 6, what is the domain of the function h(x) = f(g(x))?
questions.explanation: The composition is h(x) = √(x − 6), and a square root requires a nonnegative input: x − 6 ≥ 0, so x ≥ 6. Choice x ≥ 0 is the domain of f alone, ignoring the inner function.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, solveset, S, Interval, oo
x = symbols("x", real=True)
dom = solveset(x - 6 >= 0, x, S.Reals)
c = {"x ≥ 6": Interval(6, oo), "x ≥ 0": Interval(0, oo),
     "x ≥ −6": Interval(-6, oo), "All real numbers": S.Reals}
[k for k, v in c.items() if v == dom][0]

questions.stem: If f(x) = 4x − 7, what is the value of f(5)?
questions.explanation: Substitute 5 for x: f(5) = 4(5) − 7 = 20 − 7 = 13. Choice 27 adds 7 instead of subtracting, and 20 stops at 4(5).

questions.stem: If g(x) = x² + 3x − 10, what is the value of g(−4)?
The function f is defined by f(x) = 2x + 1 for x < 3 and by f(x) = x² − 4 for x ≥ 3. What is the value of f(3)?
questions.explanation: Since 3 satisfies x ≥ 3, use the second rule: f(3) = 3² − 4 = 5. Choice 7 uses the rule 2x + 1, which applies only when x < 3.

questions.stem: If f(x) = x² − 5x, which of the following is an expression for f(a + 1)?
questions.explanation: Substitute a + 1 for x: f(a + 1) = (a + 1)² − 5(a + 1) = a² + 2a + 1 − 5a − 5 = a² − 3a − 4. Choice a² − 5a − 4 drops the middle term 2a from (a + 1)², and a² + 2a − 4 forgets to distribute −5 to a.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, expand
a = symbols("a")
f = lambda u: u**2 - 5*u
truth = expand(f(a + 1))
c = {"a² − 5a − 4": a**2 - 5*a - 4, "a² + 2a − 4": a**2 + 2*a - 4,
     "a² − 3a − 4": a**2 - 3*a - 4, "a² − 3a − 6": a**2 - 3*a - 6}
[k for k, v in c.items() if expand(v - truth) == 0][0]

questions.stem: If h(x) = (2x + 6)/(x − 1), what is the value of h(4)?
questions.explanation: Substitute 4 into both parts: h(4) = (2(4) + 6)/(4 − 1) = 14/3. Choice 10/3 forgets to double 4 in the numerator, and 14/5 uses x + 1 in the denominator.

questions.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = 3x − 4. If f(a) = 17, what is the value of a?
questions.explanation: Set 3a − 4 = 17. Adding 4 gives 3a = 21, so a = 7. Choice 13/3 subtracts 4 instead of adding it, and 47 evaluates f(17) rather than solving f(a) = 17.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, Eq, solve
a = symbols("a")
f = lambda t: 3*t - 4
int(solve(Eq(f(a), 17), a)[0])

questions.stem: If f(x) = x² + 3, which of the following is an expression for f(2x)?
questions.explanation: Replace x with 2x: f(2x) = (2x)² + 3 = 4x² + 3. Choice 2x² + 3 squares only x and not the 2, and 2x² + 6 is 2·f(x), which multiplies the output rather than the input.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, expand
x = symbols("x")
f = lambda u: u**2 + 3
truth = expand(f(2*x))
c = {"2x² + 3": 2*x**2 + 3, "4x² + 3": 4*x**2 + 3,
     "2x² + 6": 2*x**2 + 6, "4x² + 6": 4*x**2 + 6}
[k for k, v in c.items() if expand(v - truth) == 0][0]

questions.stem: If f(x) = |x − 3| + 2, what is the value of f(−1)?
questions.explanation: Substitute −1: f(−1) = |−1 − 3| + 2 = |−4| + 2 = 4 + 2 = 6. Choice −2 skips the absolute value, and 4 forgets to add 2.

questions.stem: For the function f(x) = x², what is the value of (f(5) − f(3))/(5 − 3)?
questions.explanation: Evaluate the function first: f(5) = 25 and f(3) = 9. Then (25 − 9)/(5 − 3) = 16/2 = 8, the average rate of change of f from 3 to 5. Choice 16 forgets to divide by 5 − 3, and 4 evaluates f(5 − 3).

questions.stem: For the function f(x) = kx² + 3, where k is a constant, f(2) = 19. What is the value of k?
questions.explanation: Substitute x = 2: k(2)² + 3 = 19, so 4k = 16 and k = 4. Choice 8 divides 16 by 2 instead of by 2² = 4, and 16 forgets to divide at all.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, Eq, solve
k = symbols("k")
f = lambda t: k*t**2 + 3
int(solve(Eq(f(2), 19), k)[0])

questions.stem: The graph of y = x² is shifted 6 units up in the standard (x, y) coordinate plane. Which of the following is an equation of the resulting graph?
questions.explanation: A vertical shift up adds a constant outside the squaring: y = x² + 6. Writing (x + 6)² or (x − 6)² would shift the graph horizontally, and x² − 6 shifts it down.

questions.stem: The point (2, 5) lies on the graph of y = f(x). Which of the following points must lie on the graph of y = f(x) + 3?
questions.explanation: Adding 3 outside the function shifts every point up 3 units, so the y-coordinate changes from 5 to 8 while x stays 2. The new point is (2, 8). Changing x instead would correspond to a horizontal shift.

questions.stem: The graph of y = √x is reflected across the x-axis. Which of the following is an equation of the resulting graph?
questions.explanation: Reflecting a graph across the x-axis multiplies every output by −1, giving y = −√x. Replacing x with −x, as in √(−x), would reflect across the y-axis instead.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, sqrt, simplify
x = symbols("x")
truth = -sqrt(x)
c = {"y = √(−x)": sqrt(-x), "y = 1/√x": 1/sqrt(x),
     "y = −√x": -sqrt(x), "y = −√(−x)": -sqrt(-x)}
[k for k, v in c.items() if simplify(v - truth) == 0][0]

questions.stem: In the standard (x, y) coordinate plane, the graph of y = |x| is shifted 4 units to the right and 3 units up. What is the vertex of the resulting graph?
questions.explanation: The vertex of y = |x| is (0, 0). Shifting 4 units right moves the x-coordinate to 4, and shifting 3 units up moves the y-coordinate to 3, so the new vertex is (4, 3).

questions.stem: The graph of y = g(x) is the graph of y = f(x) compressed horizontally toward the y-axis so that each point of the graph moves to half its original distance from the y-axis. Which of the following equations defines g(x)?
questions.explanation: If the point (t, f(t)) moves to (t/2, f(t)), then g(t/2) must equal f(t), which happens when g(x) = f(2x). Using f(x/2) stretches the graph horizontally instead, and 2f(x) or (1/2)f(x) changes the outputs rather than the inputs.

questions.stem: The height of the water at a harbor, in feet, t hours after midnight is given by h(t). At a second harbor, the water reaches each height 2 hours later than at the first harbor, and every height is 3 feet greater. Which of the following functions gives the height of the water, in feet, at the second harbor t hours after midnight?
questions.explanation: A 2-hour delay means the second harbor at time t matches the first harbor at time t − 2, which replaces t with t − 2. Heights 3 feet greater add 3 outside the function, giving h(t − 2) + 3. Using h(t + 2) would make the tide arrive 2 hours earlier instead of later.
questions.verify:
h = lambda t: t*t - 5*t + 20
g = lambda t: h(t - 2) + 3
c = {"h(t + 2) + 3": lambda t: h(t+2)+3, "h(t + 2) − 3": lambda t: h(t+2)-3, "h(t − 2) − 3": lambda t: h(t-2)-3, "h(t − 2) + 3": lambda t: h(t-2)+3}
[k for k, q in c.items() if all(q(t) == g(t) for t in (0, 1, 3, 7))][0]

questions.stem: The graph of y = f(x) is reflected across the y-axis and then shifted 1 unit down. Which of the following equations defines the resulting graph?
questions.explanation: A reflection across the y-axis replaces x with −x, giving f(−x), and shifting 1 unit down subtracts 1 from the output. The result is y = f(−x) − 1. Writing −f(x) would reflect across the x-axis instead.
questions.verify:
f = lambda t: t**3 + 2*t + 5
truth = lambda x: f(-x) - 1
c = {"y = −f(x) − 1": lambda x: -f(x) - 1,
     "y = f(−x) − 1": lambda x: f(-x) - 1,
     "y = f(−x) + 1": lambda x: f(-x) + 1,
     "y = −f(x − 1)": lambda x: -f(x - 1)}
[k for k, g in c.items() if all(g(t) == truth(t) for t in (-2, -1, 0, 1, 3))][0]

questions.stem: The graph of y = f(x) is stretched vertically by a factor of 3 and then shifted 2 units down. Which of the following equations defines the resulting graph?
questions.explanation: A vertical stretch by a factor of 3 multiplies the output by 3, giving 3f(x), and the shift down then subtracts 2: y = 3f(x) − 2. Applying the shift before the stretch gives 3(f(x) − 2) = 3f(x) − 6, and f(3x) changes the input instead of the output.
questions.verify:
f = lambda x: x*x - 4*x + 5
g = lambda x: 3*f(x) - 2
c = {"y = 3f(x − 2)": lambda x: 3*f(x-2), "y = f(3x) − 2": lambda x: f(3*x)-2, "y = 3f(x) − 2": lambda x: 3*f(x)-2, "y = 3(f(x) − 2)": lambda x: 3*(f(x)-2)}
[k for k, q in c.items() if all(abs(q(t) - g(t)) < 1e-9 for t in (0, 1, 2, -3))][0]

questions.stem: The graph of y = 2^x is shifted 3 units to the left and 2 units down. What is the y-coordinate of the y-intercept of the resulting graph?
questions.explanation: The new equation is y = 2^(x + 3) − 2. At x = 0, y = 2³ − 2 = 8 − 2 = 6. Forgetting the downward shift gives 8, and shifting right instead of left gives 2^(−3) − 2 = −15/8.

questions.stem: The function g is defined by g(x) = −f(x − 4) + 6. The point (1, 3) lies on the graph of y = f(x). Which of the following points must lie on the graph of y = g(x)?
questions.explanation: The transformation shifts the graph 4 units right, reflects it across the x-axis, and shifts it 6 units up. So x = 1 + 4 = 5, and y = −(3) + 6 = 3, giving the point (5, 3). Forgetting the reflection gives (5, 9), and shifting left gives x = −3.

questions.stem: In △ABC, the measure of ∠B is 50°, the measure of ∠C is 60°, and b = 12. Which of the following equations follows directly from the law of sines?
questions.explanation: The law of sines says each side divided by the sine of its opposite angle is constant: b/sin B = c/sin C. Since b = 12 is opposite ∠B = 50° and c is opposite ∠C = 60°, the equation is 12/sin 50° = c/sin 60°. Pairing each side with the wrong angle's sine is the standard mismatch error.
questions.verify:
import math
s = lambda d: math.sin(math.radians(d))
co = lambda d: math.cos(math.radians(d))
b = 12
c_side = b * s(60) / s(50)
c = {"12/sin 50° = c/sin 60°": (b/s(50), c_side/s(60)),
     "12/sin 60° = c/sin 50°": (b/s(60), c_side/s(50)),
     "12 sin 50° = c sin 60°": (b*s(50), c_side*s(60)),
     "12/cos 50° = c/cos 60°": (b/co(50), c_side/co(60))}
[k for k, (l, r) in c.items() if abs(l - r) < 1e-9][0]

questions.stem: In △ABC, AB = 5, BC = 3, and the measure of ∠B is 120°. What is the length of AC?
questions.explanation: By the law of cosines, AC² = 5² + 3² − 2(5)(3)cos 120° = 25 + 9 − 30(−1/2) = 34 + 15 = 49, so AC = 7. Treating cos 120° as +1/2 gives √19, and dropping the cosine term entirely gives √34.

questions.stem: In △ABC, sin A = 3/5, sin B = 1/2, and a = 12. What is the length of side b?
questions.explanation: By the law of sines, a/sin A = b/sin B, so 12/(3/5) = 20 is the common ratio. Then b = 20 · (1/2) = 10. Multiplying 12 by sin A/sin B instead gives 72/5, and stopping at the common ratio gives 20.
questions.verify:
from fractions import Fraction
int(12 / Fraction(3, 5) * Fraction(1, 2))

questions.stem: The sides of a triangle measure 5, 7, and 8. What is the measure of the angle opposite the side of length 7?
questions.explanation: By the law of cosines, cos θ = (5² + 8² − 7²)/(2 · 5 · 8) = 40/80 = 1/2, so θ = 60°. A sign error in the numerator leads to cos θ = −1/2 and the wrong answer 120°.

questions.stem: In △DEF, DE = 12, DF = 15, and the measure of ∠D is 40°. Which of the following expressions gives the length of EF?
questions.explanation: Side EF is opposite the known angle ∠D, so the law of cosines gives EF² = 12² + 15² − 2(12)(15)cos 40°. Taking the square root yields the answer. The distractors add instead of subtract the cosine term, use sine in place of cosine, or subtract 15².
questions.verify:
import math
d = math.radians(40)
ex, ey = 12.0, 0.0
fx, fy = 15*math.cos(d), 15*math.sin(d)
ef = math.hypot(fx - ex, fy - ey)
c = {"√(12² + 15² + 2(12)(15)cos 40°)": math.sqrt(144 + 225 + 2*12*15*math.cos(d)),
     "√(12² + 15² − 2(12)(15)sin 40°)": math.sqrt(144 + 225 - 2*12*15*math.sin(d)),
     "√(12² − 15² − 2(12)(15)cos 40°)": float("nan"),
     "√(12² + 15² − 2(12)(15)cos 40°)": math.sqrt(144 + 225 - 2*12*15*math.cos(d))}
[k for k, v in c.items() if abs(v - ef) < 1e-9][0]

questions.stem: Two straight roads leave the same intersection, and the angle between them measures 70°. Maria drives 3 miles along one road, and Liam drives 4 miles along the other. To the nearest tenth of a mile, how far apart are they?
questions.explanation: The distance d satisfies d² = 3² + 4² − 2(3)(4)cos 70° ≈ 25 − 8.21 = 16.79, so d ≈ 4.1 miles. Ignoring the cosine term gives 5.0, and adding it instead of subtracting gives about 5.8.

questions.stem: In △ABC, a = 10, b = 10√2, and the measure of ∠A is 30°. Given that ∠B is acute, what is the measure of ∠B?
questions.explanation: By the law of sines, sin B = b sin A/a = 10√2 · (1/2)/10 = √2/2. Since ∠B is acute, ∠B = 45°. The obtuse solution 135° also satisfies sin B = √2/2 but is ruled out by the given condition.

questions.stem: In △RST, the measure of ∠R is 45°, the measure of ∠S is 60°, and r = 8. What is the length of side s?
questions.explanation: By the law of sines, s = r sin S/sin R = 8(√3/2)/(√2/2) = 8√3/√2 = 4√6. Flipping the ratio and computing 8 sin 45°/sin 60° gives 8√6/3 instead.
questions.verify:
import math
v = 8*math.sin(math.radians(60))/math.sin(math.radians(45))
"4√6" if abs(v - 4*math.sqrt(6)) < 1e-9 else "mismatch"

questions.stem: A triangle has sides of lengths 4, 6, and 8. What is the cosine of the largest angle of the triangle?
questions.explanation: The largest angle is opposite the longest side, 8. By the law of cosines, cos θ = (4² + 6² − 8²)/(2 · 4 · 6) = −12/48 = −1/4. Dropping the negative sign gives 1/4, while 7/8 and 11/16 are the cosines of the angles opposite the sides of lengths 4 and 6.
questions.verify:
from fractions import Fraction
f = Fraction(4**2 + 6**2 - 8**2, 2*4*6)
("−" if f < 0 else "") + f"{abs(f.numerator)}/{abs(f.denominator)}"

questions.stem: A surveyor standing at point A sights a boulder at point B and a flagpole at point C. She measures the angle ∠BAC as 55°, the angle ∠ABC as 65°, and the distance AC as 120 meters. To the nearest meter, what is the distance BC?
questions.explanation: Side BC is opposite ∠A and side AC = 120 is opposite ∠B, so the law of sines gives BC = 120 sin 55°/sin 65° ≈ 108 meters. Multiplying by sin 55° without dividing by sin 65° gives 98, and flipping the ratio gives 133.

questions.stem: If −6x = 42, then x = ?
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by −6: x = 42/(−6) = −7. Dropping the negative sign gives 7, subtracting 6 from 42 gives 36, and multiplying instead of dividing gives 252.

questions.stem: If 2x + 5 = 17, what is the value of 3x − 4 ?
questions.explanation: First solve for x: 2x = 12, so x = 6. Then 3x − 4 = 3(6) − 4 = 14. Stopping at x = 6 or reporting 3x = 18 leaves the substitution unfinished.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, Eq, solve, Rational, sqrt, nsimplify
x = symbols("x")
x0 = solve(Eq(2*x + 5, 17), x)[0]
int(3*x0 - 4)

questions.stem: What value of x satisfies the equation 2(3x + 1) = 5x + 9 ?
questions.explanation: Distribute on the left: 6x + 2 = 5x + 9. Subtracting 5x and then 2 gives x = 7. Forgetting to distribute the 2 to the 1 leads to 6x + 1 = 5x + 9 and the wrong answer 8.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, Eq, solve, Rational, sqrt, nsimplify
x = symbols("x")
int(solve(Eq(2*(3*x + 1), 5*x + 9), x)[0])

questions.stem: If (2x − 5)/3 = 7, then x = ?
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by 3: 2x − 5 = 21. Then 2x = 26, so x = 13. Solving 2x − 5 = 7 without clearing the fraction gives 6, and forgetting to divide by 2 leaves 26.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, Eq, solve, Rational, sqrt, nsimplify
x = symbols("x")
int(solve(Eq((2*x - 5)/3, 7), x)[0])

questions.explanation: Subtract 1.2 from both sides to get 0.4x = 2.4, then divide by 0.4 to get x = 6. Stopping at 2.4 skips the division, and adding 1.2 instead of subtracting gives 12.

questions.stem: A taxi ride costs $3 plus $2 for each mile traveled. If a ride costs $19 in total, how many miles long was the ride?
questions.explanation: The equation is 3 + 2m = 19, so 2m = 16 and m = 8 miles. Dividing the full $19 by $2 gives 9.5, which ignores the $3 base fare, and adding the fare instead of subtracting gives 11.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, Eq, solve
m = symbols("m")
int(solve(Eq(3 + 2*m, 19), m)[0])

questions.stem: If x/2 − x/5 = 9, then x = ?
questions.explanation: Combine the fractions: x/2 − x/5 = 5x/10 − 2x/10 = 3x/10. So 3x/10 = 9, which gives x = 30. Treating the left side as x/3 gives 27, and multiplying 9 by just one denominator gives 18 or 45.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, Eq, solve, Rational, sqrt, nsimplify
x = symbols("x")
int(solve(Eq(x/2 - x/5, 9), x)[0])

questions.explanation: Distribute: 4x − 8 − 3x − 3 = 10, so x − 11 = 10 and x = 21. Failing to distribute the negative to the 1 gives 4x − 8 − 3x + 3 = 10 and the wrong answer 15.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, Eq, solve, Rational, sqrt, nsimplify
x = symbols("x")
int(solve(Eq(4*(x - 2) - 3*(x + 1), 10), x)[0])

questions.stem: If ax + b = c, where a ≠ 0, which of the following expresses x in terms of a, b, and c?
questions.explanation: Subtract b from both sides to get ax = c − b, then divide both sides by a: x = (c − b)/a. Adding b instead of subtracting, reversing the subtraction, or dividing only b by a all give incorrect forms.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, solve, simplify
x, a, b, c0 = symbols("x a b c", positive=True)
truth = solve(a*x + b - c0, x)[0]
c = {"x = (c − b)/a": (c0 - b)/a, "x = (c + b)/a": (c0 + b)/a,
     "x = (b − c)/a": (b - c0)/a, "x = c − b/a": c0 - b/a}
[k for k, v in c.items() if simplify(v - truth) == 0][0]

questions.explanation: Cross-multiply: 2(2x − 1) = 3(x + 4), so 4x − 2 = 3x + 12. Subtracting 3x and adding 2 gives x = 14. Cross-multiplying with the wrong pairs gives 6x − 3 = 2x + 8 and the answer 11/4.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, Eq, solve, Rational, sqrt, nsimplify
x = symbols("x")
int(solve(Eq((2*x - 1)/3, (x + 4)/2), x)[0])

questions.stem: What is the slope of the line that passes through the points (1, 4) and (5, 16) in the standard (x, y) coordinate plane?
questions.explanation: Slope is the change in y over the change in x: (16 − 4)/(5 − 1) = 12/4 = 3. Inverting the ratio gives 1/3, and using only the change in y gives 12.

questions.stem: The linear function f has slope −2, and f(0) = 7. Which of the following defines f(x)?
questions.explanation: In slope-intercept form f(x) = mx + b, the slope m is −2 and the value f(0) = 7 is the y-intercept b. So f(x) = −2x + 7. Swapping the roles of 7 and −2 gives f(x) = 7x − 2.
questions.verify:
m, b = -2, 7
truth = lambda x: m*x + b
c = {"f(x) = −2x + 7": lambda x: -2*x + 7, "f(x) = −2x − 7": lambda x: -2*x - 7,
     "f(x) = 2x + 7": lambda x: 2*x + 7, "f(x) = 7x − 2": lambda x: 7*x - 2}
[k for k, f in c.items() if all(f(t) == truth(t) for t in (-3, 0, 1, 4))][0]

questions.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = 5x + 3. For what value of x is f(x) = 43?
questions.explanation: Set 5x + 3 = 43. Subtracting 3 gives 5x = 40, so x = 8. Adding 3 instead of subtracting gives 9.2, and substituting 43 for x gives 218.
questions.verify:
from sympy import symbols, Eq, solve, Rational, sqrt, nsimplify
x = symbols("x")
f = lambda t: 5*t + 3
int(solve(Eq(f(x), 43), x)[0])

questions.stem: The total cost, in dollars, of taking x pottery classes at a studio is given by C(x) = 15x + 60. Which of the following situations does this function describe?
choices: The studio charges a one-time $15 fee plus $60 for each class.
The studio charges $75 for each class.
The studio charges $60 for each class and gives a one-time $15 discount.
The studio charges a one-time $60 fee plus $15 for each class.
questions.explanation: In C(x) = 15x + 60 the coefficient 15 is multiplied by the number of classes, so it is the per-class charge, and the constant 60 is added only once, so it is a one-time fee. Swapping the roles of 15 and 60 or combining them into a single rate of 75 misreads the model.
questions.verify:
C = lambda x: 15*x + 60

questions.stem: The value, in dollars, of a delivery van t years after purchase is modeled by V(t) = 32,000 − 2,400t. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number 2,400 in this model?
choices: The van's value increases by $2,400 each year.
The van's value decreases by $2,400 each year.
The van was worth $2,400 when it was purchased.
The van's value decreases by $32,000 each year.
questions.explanation: The coefficient of t is the rate of change of the value per year, and the negative sign means the value goes down. So the van loses $2,400 in value each year. The purchase price is the constant term, $32,000.
questions.verify:
Vt = lambda t: 32000 - 2400*t
yearly = Vt(1) - Vt(0)
